title: Iran-Contra Affair: Shady in the 80s, Part 2
summary: Part two of the Iran-Contra Affair series. The hosts explain how the Reagan administration, after Congress cut off funding, secretly sold TOW missiles to Iran in exchange for American hostages held by Lebanese terrorists, then diverted the profits to fund the Contras fighting the Sandinistas in Nicaragua. They cover the Israeli and CIA-run arms shipments, Oliver North's role, the October 1986 supply plane shootdown and capture of Eugene Hasenfus, the exposure of the scandal, the shredding of documents, the investigations, convictions and reversals, Bush's pardons, and Reagan's approval rebound. The episode also includes ad reads, off-topic banter about the 1980s and the August tour dates, and a listener mail segment about the Apollo missions.

segments.title: Live tour promo and opening
segments.summary: Hosts promote upcoming live show dates at the State Theater in Portland, Maine, then open the episode.

segments.title: Iran enters the picture and the 1979 hostage crisis
segments.summary: Recap of the Contra funding cutoff, then background on Iran after the 1979 revolution, the American embassy hostage crisis, its release around Reagan's inauguration, and Lebanese terrorists holding Americans while Reagan refused to negotiate with terrorists.

segments.title: Eighties nostalgia tangent
segments.summary: Casual banter about 1980s pop culture, TWA Flight 847 hijacking memories, and the hosts' band plans.

segments.title: Israel and Iran arms deal
segments.summary: Israel's history of hostage exchanges leads to Reagan administration secretly offering arms to Iran, which was fighting Iraq, while the US was publicly supporting Iraq. Oliver North is brought in and travels to Iran under an alias; he deals with Iranian businessman Ghorbanifar, whom the CIA had burned.

segments.title: TOW missile shipments and the diversion of funds
segments.summary: Israel shipped 508 TOW missiles to Iran and a hostage was released. The operation was then run by the US through the CIA, Richard Secord, and Ghorbanifar, with markups. About 2,000 missiles were sent in eight shipments, and profits were diverted to fund the Contras.

segments.title: Congress funding and the Contra resupply
segments.summary: Congress later approved a hundred million dollars for the Contras, though covert activity continued. Hosts discuss the October 1986 cargo plane shot down over Nicaragua.

segments.title: Shootdown, Hasenfus capture, and exposure
segments.summary: The October 1986 supply plane was shot down by Sandinistas. Eugene Hasenfus survived with a borrowed parachute, was captured, and talked. Documents tied the flights to Southern Air Transport, a CIA front, and to Robert Owen and North. A Soldier of Fortune party boast, a whistleblower affidavit, and a Lebanese newspaper report exposed the scandal.

segments.title: Aftermath, investigations, and pardons
segments.summary: North and Fawn Hall shredded documents; the administration blamed John Poindexter and North as a rogue actor. Reagan denied then partially admitted the Iran deal. The Tower Commission, convictions and reversals, Bush's Christmas Eve pardons, Walsh's comments on the diary, and Reagan's approval rebound.

segments.title: Listener mail: Apollo missions
segments.summary: A listener discusses Apollo's separated command module and lunar lander, and the Apollo 8 mission. The hosts thank him and sign off.
